name: vrl-tools
description: Highlighting, snippets and Vector config support for VRL (Vector Remap Language).

commands.title: Go to component and follow its paths
Mark output as terminal in the settings

vrl-tools.useSampleEventForDiagnostics.markdownDescription: Type each program against the sample event next to it (`program.vrl.sample.json`), when there is one. The compiler then knows the fields your events actually carry, which turns "this might fail" into "this field does not exist". Turn it off to always check against an event of unknown shape.

vrl-tools.vectorConfig.markdownDescription: The files your Vector reads its config from, as the patterns you pass to `vector --config`, relative to the workspace folder — for example `config/**/*.toml`. They are read as one pipeline: the graph draws all of them, and enrichment lookups are checked against the tables they declare. Each is loaded on its own, as `--config` does, so a file that only adds to a component declared in another (a `[[transforms.x.routes]]` with no `type`) is an error; if that is how your config is written, Vector is started with `--config-dir` and `#vrl-tools.vectorConfigDir#` is the setting. Left empty with that one, every YAML or TOML file in the workspace that declares `sources`, `transforms`, `sinks` or `enrichment_tables` is used.

vrl-tools.vectorConfigDir.markdownDescription: The directories your Vector reads its config from, as you pass them to `vector --config-dir`, relative to the workspace folder — for example `config`. The YAML, TOML and JSON files directly in each are merged into one config, as Vector merges them, so one component can be written across files: a router in one, each route added from its own. Read together with `#vrl-tools.vectorConfig#` as one pipeline. The `sources/`, `transforms/`… subfolders of a config directory are not read yet.

vrl-tools.terminalOutputs.markdownDescription: Outputs that are meant to end where they are: nothing reads them, on purpose. Each entry is an output as an input would name it (`route_by_product._unmatched`) or a component (`dropped-handler`, every output it has), with the wildcards `inputs` takes (`*._unmatched`). The graph draws these as an end instead of reporting "nothing reads …". The same can be said in the config itself, with a `# vrl-tools: terminal` comment on the line that declares the component or the route — add `_unmatched` or `dropped` after it for an output that has no line of its own. Vector knows nothing of either and still prints its own warning.

vrl-tools.componentNamePattern.markdownDescription: A naming convention for the components of a pipeline, off unless set: a regular expression per component `type` that the names of components of that type should match, for example `{ "remap": "^[a-z0-9_]+-normalizer$" }`. A name that does not match is reported as information, never as a warning — Vector runs the config whatever a component is called. The expressions are unanchored unless they anchor themselves, and have no lookaround or backreferences.
